available_roles: Insight and Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence) - Analyst, Senior Analyst & Specialist

selection_insights.test_details: Most candidates reported a single online aptitude test used mainly for interview shortlisting. Topics covered varied across responses and included reasoning, quantitative/math, comprehension, statistics, English, basic graph analysis and probability. Difficulty was generally described as basic to moderate. One candidate's preparation tip: practiced 10 aptitude tests and solved 50+ puzzles before the test.
selection_insights.interview_details: Most candidates went through 2 interview rounds. A common pattern: the first round included a guesstimate and a case study along with basic resume questions, while the second round focused more on the resume (internships, projects) and HR questions, often described as relaxed/conversational. Some candidates reported a purely resume + HR style interview with no case at all (including a few AI-related questions). One candidate interviewed separately for Accenture India and Accenture Global, with both rounds focused on resume and cases.
questions_asked: Why consulting?
Where do you see yourself in 5s?
Do you want to do an MBA?
Why do you think you are suitable for this role?
Guesstimate: how many cars are purchased in Mumbai every month
Case study: a basic FMCG case where revenue is decreasing and costs are increasing
A few questions on AI
General HR questions, felt more like a conversation than a formal interview

(Reported by a candidate who also interviewed at Mckinsey, Bain, BCG, LEK and Strategy& the same season) 2 case interviews including a guesstimate on the number of electric buses in Mumbai, and questions related to the candidate's core engineering department
recommended_electives_projects: Entrepreneurial Venture elective was specifically called out as effective in getting shortlisted and then selected. A product management internship on the resume was also mentioned as helpful during the interview discussion.

companies.name: Boston Consulting Group (BCG)

selection_insights.test_details: Most candidates reported no formal written or online test. Selection ran through informal 'buddy rounds' followed by final case interviews after shortlisting. One candidate noted that Interest Application Forms (IAFs) were filled for all 'Day 1' consulting companies and Morgan Stanley, and that only Morgan Stanley required an aptitude test — the consulting firms themselves had none.
selection_insights.interview_details: Most candidates went through 2 buddy rounds before the main interview, with buddy rounds focused purely on case practice (no HR questions). On the interview day itself, candidates had 2 case interviews of around 40 minutes each — the first was purely case-based, while the second added HR questions alongside the case. One candidate also described McKinsey's parallel process for comparison: 3 buddy rounds (2 focused only on cases, 1 mixing case practice with basic HR/resume questions), followed by a single final interview combining HR questions with a market-growth case.
questions_asked: Case: A global tool manufacturer has entered India and has not achieved the same success as the rest of the world – why, and how to solve this
Case: Post-UPI rollout, bank ATMs have lost relevance – how do you decide if any ATM should close or remain operational
HR: pick something from your resume and elaborate on it
Tell me something unique about yourself
(From the same candidate, describing McKinsey's process) Market growth case in the final interview round

(Reported by a candidate who also interviewed at Mckinsey, Bain, LEK, Strategy& and Accenture the same season) 2 case interviews including a guesstimate on the number of electric buses in Mumbai, and questions related to the candidate's core engineering department
recommended_electives_projects: NA – no specific electives or projects were mentioned.

Mental Math: Calculate the 95% confidence interval of a Poisson process given observed arrivals under time constraints.

companies.name: Texas Instruments

selection_insights.test_details:
1. There was a single test of 2 hours with 3 sections. Two sections of 45 minutes each for the core domains that you have applied for (Analog/Digital/Signal Processing/Embedded), followed by 30 minutes aptitude section.

2. Two tests; purely technical; one for analog and one for signals. Got shortlisted in both.

3. Aptitude, Analog, Digital
selection_insights.interview_details:
1. An interview for each of the domains you have been shortlisted for after the test. Typical interview time is 30 minutes to an hour. Mostly technical questions with a few general HR questions at the end.

2. There were two interviews; one for each profile I was shortlisted for, analog and signal processing. 

3. Analog, Digital
questions_asked: Around 15 minutes were spent on my resume points alone. Then questions from multiple domains like signal processing, control system and digital systems were asked. Can't recollect the exact questions right now.
Analog Interview: Mostly the questions were based on capacitor charging/discharging circuits. And some BJT and MoSFET questions. Mostly the basics.
Signals Interview: Focused on Nyquist rule of bandwidth and sampling frequencies.
recommended_electives_projects: EE 224: Digital Systems EE 309: Microprocessors EE 214: Digital Circuits Lab EE 337: Microprocessors Laboratory EE 671: VLSI Design (done in 5th sem)

companies.name: Adobe

selection_insights.test_details:
In summers, grasp as much concept as you can by solving dsa questions. I did striver A2Z sheet, around 400+ questions.. Number of test don't matter tbh, I did not give 10+ contest or anything mostly 5 only before intern test started. Focus on ML topics for projects, some websites projects , hackathons are really a good source for projects too. If you are targetting quant too, then do brainstellar probability questions. Some tests focus on OS, Dbms, oops networks too but only some of them. Main questions are based on DP, greedy, graphs, arrays, strings. Also do remember all libraries which you need to import, sometimes tests tell you to write full code from scratch instead of just writing a function. Mainly focus on filling your resume and DSA if you are targetting software roles (doesn't matter ML or Software or product) , everyone mostly asks DSA..Some may ask mcq on ML like bias variance regularisation, or training ML models but low in number.

2.1 OA (3 dsa questions + core cs theory(cpp, python, OS, dbms, java))

3. All the software and quant companies will usually have an initial DSA test consisting of some probability questions and DSA questions. Most important topics in DSA would be DP, Sliding Window, 2-Pointer Algorithm and Graphs, mostly all the tests did have at least one question from DP.
selection_insights.interview_details:
Usally tech companies have 1 tech interview round and 1 HR round or combined. Adobe Product was combined. For tech rounds, prepare DSA mainly again. They ask your resume projects which stand out the most, so for resume for each project do know What, Why, How of each project and your impact basically. Your strength weakness and any previous work experience, what did you learn from it and why do you want to join this role..All these questions you should know.

2. 1 hour interview (3 dsa questions, 5 min resume, 5 min core cs theory(basic))

3.  1 Interview: They asked everything, DSA, System Design, Resume, Problem Solving and HR in the same interview, it was around 1.5 hours.
questions_asked: DSA: DP, greedy, Array+strings, Trees+graphs, heaps ML: bias variance tradeoff, regularization, training a model, accuracy precision recall f1 score , deep NN Networks, DB, OS OOPS (in case of Sony Japan)
recommended_electives_projects:
1. DS203 CS419 To be honest any course with tech projects is good. Do hackathons or competitions for more projects to differentiate in the crowd.


2. DS203
CS207 (they didnt help directly but helped in understanding related concepts)

companies.name: Amazon

selection_insights.test_details:
1. One Online Assessment 
2. 2 questions in test and 2 in interview. Trees, graphs, dynamic programming and 2 pointers
selection_insights.interview_details: After the OA there was only one technical interview.
questions_asked: There was a single OA divided into two sections. The first was a coding assessment consisting of two leetcode medium-to-hard level DSA questions. The second section featured HR questions based on real-world scenarios, which needed to be answered with Amazon's Leadership Principles in mind. In the interview, I was given two DSA problems. The first was a dynamic programming question (Longest Common Subsequence) based on Amazon reviews. The second was a graph problem (BFS) that, when analyzed correctly, could actually be simplified into basic matrix operations (which was the optimal solution they were looking for).
1 round: Leetcode hard problems, 1 was rainwater trapping and other was string palindrome, dynamic programming problem, leetcode medium.
